rules.name: Unresolved conversion block needs review
rules.short_description: A RESOLVE EWI block marks code that needs manual conversion before execution.
rules.long_description:
SnowConvert inserts !!!RESOLVE EWI!!! where code needs manual work. In executable SQL, this marker is intended to make Snowflake compilation fail. A marker found in a comment or other non-executed text does not by itself prove a compilation failure.

dbt compile renders executable SQL but does not materialize the model. Successful rendering alone does not prove that the warehouse accepts the SQL or that the result matches the source. Retaining a resolved marker as a reviewed record is a local migration-policy choice.

## References

- [SnowConvert AI - Understanding Converted Code](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/migrations/snowconvert-docs/general/technical-documentation/issues-and-troubleshooting/README)
- [About dbt compile command](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/commands/compile)
- [About dbt build command](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/commands/build)
rules.remediation: Read the issue message and the original source expression. Implement the required behavior, then remove the executable marker. Compile the affected model to inspect its SQL. Build and test it in a controlled target, and compare relevant results with the source. Preserve review evidence before removing historical comments; deleting the marker alone does not fix the conversion.

examples.title: Unresolved EWI block

rules.name: Conversion issue marker remains in the model
rules.short_description: A SnowConvert SSC-EWI code remains and needs a recorded resolution or review decision.
rules.long_description:
An EWI identifies code that SnowConvert could not fully convert or verify. A remaining marker is a reason to review that issue. It does not prove that no one has already validated the model.

This rule treats retained markers as unresolved until they are removed or waived under the project's migration policy. The code reference explains the conversion issue; the project decides how to record its resolution.

## References

- [SnowConvert AI - Understanding Converted Code](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/migrations/snowconvert-docs/general/technical-documentation/issues-and-troubleshooting/README)
rules.remediation: Look up the exact code for the source platform and converter version. Compare the affected behavior with the original system, including relevant edge cases. Add a regression test. Remove a resolved marker only after preserving the evidence, or keep it with a documented waiver if the project retains conversion history.

examples.title: Leftover EWI marker
examples.bad:
select a -- SSC-EWI-SSIS0004 - control flow element not converted
from {{ ref('stg_a') }}

rules.name: Functional-difference marker needs review
rules.short_description: An SSC-FDM marker identifies a possible behavior difference that needs an explicit review decision.
rules.long_description:
A SnowConvert FDM is a comment about a possible functional difference. The comment does not block compilation, so successful execution does not establish equivalence with the source system. Some differences require a business or design decision.

The rule selects advice from the marker code and text. Confirm that advice against the converter version and the original mapping. Sign-off and retention of reviewed markers are local migration policy, not dbt requirements.

## References

- [SnowConvert AI - Understanding Converted Code](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/migrations/snowconvert-docs/general/technical-documentation/issues-and-troubleshooting/README)
- [FIRST_VALUE: Usage notes](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/functions/first_value)
- [About ref function](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/dbt-jinja-functions/ref)
rules.remediation: Read context.code, the marker text, and the original mapping before changing the model. If the marker reports sequential load groups combined with UNION ALL, check whether later groups need earlier writes; separate those operations when they do. If it reports a source-and-target table, establish whether the read needs prior-run or current-run state before choosing a snapshot or ref(). For row-selection differences, define a deterministic tie-break rule. Record accepted differences and validation evidence in the model description and review record.

examples.title: Unsigned FDM marker
examples.bad:
select a -- SSC-FDM-0006 - ordering may differ
from {{ ref('stg_a') }}
examples.good:
-- Reviewed: ordering is made deterministic below.
select a
from {{ ref('stg_a') }}
order by a

rules.name: Unresolved manual conversion handoff
rules.short_description: A NEEDS-USER marker records a manual conversion action that may still be outstanding.
rules.long_description:
NEEDS-USER is a local workflow marker for a manual action. It is not a standard dbt command or an upstream SnowConvert issue category. The marker must be checked against the task it describes.

SnowConvert documents that incomplete conversions can need manual work. This rule uses the local marker to request that review; it does not determine whether the work has already been completed.

## References

- [SnowConvert AI - Understanding Converted Code](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/migrations/snowconvert-docs/general/technical-documentation/issues-and-troubleshooting/README)
rules.remediation: Check the named action and its acceptance criteria. Complete and verify the work before removing the marker. If the action is complete and the comment is retained for history, document the evidence and waive the finding under the project's policy.

examples.title: NEEDS-USER hand-off
examples.bad:
-- NEEDS-USER: map the lookup table by hand
select a from {{ ref('stg_a') }}

rules.name: ETL operation flags remain in model data
rules.short_description: etl_dml_operation__ or DD_* constants carry row-level insert, update, delete, or reject intent.
rules.long_description:
Converted ETL code can carry load instructions in a row column. Removing that column or its filters can change which rows are inserted, updated, deleted, or rejected. The rule flags this pattern for a semantic review, not automatic removal.

A supported dbt merge strategy with a valid unique_key can handle inserts and updates. It does not by itself reproduce arbitrary delete, reject, or update-only behavior. Keep the control column when a reviewed materialization still consumes it.

## References

- [About incremental strategy](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/incremental-strategy)
rules.remediation: Map each operation flag to the source behavior. Select a supported materialization for that behavior. Preserve rejection filters and NULL handling. Use merge for insert/update semantics only when appropriate. Implement required hard deletes explicitly, or use a soft-delete flag only if the business requirement permits it. Drop the control column only after all consumers are replaced and tested. The example is incomplete for delete or reject requirements.

examples.title: ETL DML control column
examples.good:
{{ config(materialized='incremental', incremental_strategy='merge', unique_key='id') }}
select * from {{ ref('stg_a') }}

rules.name: Conversion test scaffolding remains
rules.short_description: The project still contains stabilization_test artifacts.
rules.long_description:
stabilization_test is a local conversion-workflow convention. A one-time comparison can help validate a migration, but it does not replace tests for the data and business rules that must hold after deployment. A retained test can still be useful if its assertions remain valid.

The rule requests review of these artifacts; it does not measure their coverage. Retirement and waiver decisions belong to the project's migration policy.

## References

- [Add data tests to your DAG](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/data-tests)
rules.remediation: Inspect each stabilization artifact. Keep useful assertions and preserve migration validation evidence. Replace obsolete checks with data tests for the required keys, relationships, and business rules. Remove only scaffolding that no longer serves a documented purpose.

references.title: Add data tests to your DAG

rules.name: Model name retains an ETL instance prefix
rules.short_description: A model name contains an SQ_, EXP_, FIL_, LKP_, or UPDTRANS instance prefix.
rules.long_description:
ETL instance names can describe the source tool rather than the data a model produces. A business-oriented name can help readers understand the model without the original mapping. The checked prefixes are a local naming policy, not reserved or invalid dbt names.

Keep an existing name when traceability or an external interface requires it. dbt alias configuration can separate a model's resource name from its database relation name.

## References

- [alias](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/resource-configs/alias)
- [How we style our SQL](https://docs.getdbt.com/best-practices/how-we-style/2-how-we-style-our-sql)
rules.remediation: Choose a name that describes the model's data or transformation. Update refs, properties, tests, selectors, and automation that use the old resource name. Review per-transformation chains with the materialization findings before renaming every step. Use alias when the database relation name must stay stable, and test that existing consumers still work.

rules.name: Conversion placeholder model remains
rules.short_description: A placeholder comment, tag, or empty-query pattern marks a model for conversion review.
rules.long_description:
A placeholder model may return no rows while still building successfully. Tests that only search for invalid rows can pass on empty input. Other tests, such as explicit row-count checks, can detect the absence. A placeholder tag or comment alone does not prove the output is empty.

The rule uses local placeholder patterns, including a Status: placeholder comment, WHERE FALSE, or a placeholder tag, and reports a completion percentage. That percentage reflects these patterns, not verified migration completeness.

## References

- [Add data tests to your DAG](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/data-tests)
- [About dbt build command](https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/commands/build)
rules.remediation: Implement the missing logic and test expected data presence as well as value correctness. If the model is deferred, remove or disable it and update dependent models through a controlled change. Keep an intentionally empty model only with a documented purpose and suitable tests. Do not delete refs from consumers without reviewing the resulting behavior.

examples.title: Placeholder model
examples.bad:
-- Status: placeholder
select null as id where false

rules.name: Generic custom incremental strategy name
rules.short_description: A model or macro uses the custom strategy name update_only or insert_only.
rules.long_description:
A custom incremental strategy is resolved through a get_incremental_STRATEGY_sql macro. Generic names can conflict with other implementations when projects or packages are combined. A project-specific name can make ownership clearer.

The rule checks update_only and insert_only in model or folder configuration and macro definitions. It excludes delete_only under the local migration policy. These names are not invalid in dbt; the official documentation itself uses insert_only as an example. Custom-strategy support depends on the adapter and dbt version.

## References

- [About incremental strategy](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/incremental-strategy)
rules.remediation: Check the resolved strategy macro before renaming. If ownership is ambiguous, choose a project-specific strategy name and rename its get_incremental_STRATEGY_sql macro. Update all model and folder configurations together. Compile and test representative incremental and full-refresh runs. Keep a generic name when its resolution is deliberate and documented.
